issue_context.title: `ComponentRef#setInput` should return result indicating whether input was set successfully
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

(Tangentially related to #51878)

Currently, we call `setInput(name, value)` with an incorrect input name, all that will occur is a console error. This makes it impossible for the consumer to capture this error and deal with it as they wish.


### Proposed solution

Simply have `setInput()` return a boolean indicating whether the value was set properly. This should not represent a meaningful breaking change (should only affect consumers who were for some reason depending on the return type of setInput being `void`).

### Alternatives considered

N/A
comments:
I don't think this is correct. Returning a boolean just goes around the problem of not having types.
I believe something like https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/51878#issuecomment-1973757043 should be the solution.

What I meant is 99% of the cases where you are wrong about the input name or value is in development time. So a runtime validation seems too late. Unless there is a use case for it (guess some dynamic input name from server? But seems far fetched)

Thnx for the suggestion @MaximSagan - we did discuss this at length in the team and decided that we would rather focus on addressing the root cause - in this sense I can see it as duplicate of #51878.

As the API returning a boolean to indicate status - we would rather consider a breaking change (or a feature behind a flag) that throws an error instead of logging to the console.

review_comments: I'm not sure we want to be doing this since it's pretty trivial to figure this out already by looking at the property on `ComponentRef.instance`. cc @pkozlowski-opensource for a second opinion.

Yeh, I'm not a big fan of this style of error handling by returning a boolean flag.

> since it's pretty trivial to figure this out already by looking at the property on ComponentRef.instance

I'm not sure it works since `setInput` uses an aliased named and not the instance name. But checking for the presence of an input with https://angular.dev/api/core/ComponentMirror# _should_ work.

@pkozlowski-opensource 

> Yeh, I'm not a big fan of this style of error handling by returning a boolean flag.

Neither am I to be honest, but I don't see a cleaner or better way to do this without a massive breaking change. Throwing would arguably be best, but obviously can't just start throwing when we weren't throwing before.

Also, there is some precedent for returning a boolean to indicate success/failure in the Angular codebase, e.g. `router.navigate()`.

> > since it's pretty trivial to figure this out already by looking at the property on ComponentRef.instance
> 
> I'm not sure it works since `setInput` uses an aliased named and not the instance name. But checking for the presence of an input with https://angular.dev/api/core/ComponentMirror# _should_ work.

This is a bit of a roundabout way to check, isn't it? Ideally we wouldn't want to use a second API to check whether the first API succeeded.
IMO the issue is that the boolean doesn't indicate _why_ setting the input failed. E.g. did it fail because the input doesn't exist or because the value is the same as the old one?

@crisbeto

> IMO the issue is that the boolean doesn't indicate _why_ setting the input failed. E.g. did it fail because the input doesn't exist or because the value is the same as the old one?

Based on the existing implementation, there is only one mode of failure for `setInput`, and that is when the input doesn't exist.

If the value is the same as the old one, that is not really a failure in any meaningful way (and indeed the existing implementation does not even bother to log any warning in that case).

My implementation returns `false` for the former and `true` for the latter (as well as the case that the input is successfully set to a new value of course), so a result of `false` would not be ambiguous.

Excuse me for interrupting. I think why it can occur that "the input doesn't exists" is,  `ComponentRef<T>.setInput()` is not strictly typed. If `setInput()` will check the arguments types, that problem can be caught in the build time. This feature seems like a workaround against a lack of Angular's type-checking for me.
